nodes.name: 1. Webhook — Receive Batch from Web Console
nodes.notes: Web Console calls this after user confirms product + image selections. Body: { items: [{asin, title, price, pin_title, pin_description, badge_hook, image_hook, chosen_photo_url, bridge_url, hook_image_url, create_bridge_endpoint}] }

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'received', count: $json.body.items.length, message: 'Batch accepted. Processing ' + $json.body.items.length + ' products...' }) }}

nodes.name: 1b. Respond to Web Console Immediately
nodes.notes: Immediately ACK the web console so it doesn't time out. Processing continues in background.

nodes.name: 2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time
nodes.notes: Splits the incoming items array so nodes 3-5 run once per product sequentially.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ asin: $json.asin, title: $json.title, price: $json.price, pin_title: $json.pin_title, pin_description: $json.pin_description, badge_hook: $json.badge_hook, image_hook: $json.image_hook }) }}

nodes.name: 3. Build Bridge Page + Hook Image (Local Server)
nodes.notes: Calls your local Python server to: (1) generate bridge_{ASIN}.html landing page, (2) render focus_product_{ASIN}_hook.jpg with price badge overlay, (3) push both live to GitHub Pages. Returns bridge_url + hook_image_url.

string.name: final_bridge_url
string.value: ={{ $node['3. Build Bridge Page + Hook Image (Local Server)'].json.bridge_url || $node['2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time'].json.bridge_url }}

string.name: final_hook_image_url
string.value: ={{ $node['3. Build Bridge Page + Hook Image (Local Server)'].json.hook_image_url || $node['2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time'].json.hook_image_url }}

string.name: final_pin_title
string.value: ={{ $node['2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time'].json.pin_title }}

string.name: final_pin_description
string.value: ={{ $node['2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time'].json.pin_description }}

string.name: final_asin
string.value: ={{ $node['2. Split Items — Process One Product at a Time'].json.asin }}

nodes.name: 4. Merge — Combine SEO Copy + Bridge URL + Image URL
nodes.notes: Collects bridge_url from node 3 response and SEO data from node 2. All fields are now ready for the Pinterest pin POST.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ title: $json.final_pin_title.substring(0, 100), description: $json.final_pin_description.substring(0, 800), link: $json.final_bridge_url, board_id: $env.PINTEREST_BOARD_ID, media_source: { source_type: 'image_url', url: $json.final_hook_image_url } }) }}

nodes.name: 5. Post Pin to Pinterest API v5
nodes.notes: POSTs the pin to Pinterest API v5. Destination link = bridge_{ASIN}.html. Media = focus_product_{ASIN}_hook.jpg. Uses your Bearer token and Board ID from n8n env variables.

string.name: result
string.value: ={{ 'Pin posted for ' + $node['4. Merge — Combine SEO Copy + Bridge URL + Image URL'].json.final_asin + ' — Pin ID: ' + ($json.id || 'N/A') + ' | Bridge: ' + $node['4. Merge — Combine SEO Copy + Bridge URL + Image URL'].json.final_bridge_url }}

nodes.name: 6. Log Result
nodes.notes: Logs the Pin ID and bridge URL for each product. You can connect this to a Google Sheets or Telegram node for monitoring.
